name: Core digital asset allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Long-Term Digital Asset Adoption
caseLead: The investment case rests on the continued adoption of scarce digital assets as stores of value, settlement networks and collateral, allowing a diversified core allocation to participate in growth across the crypto market. The opportunity persists because network adoption remains early, institutional access is expanding, and governments are developing different rules for ownership, taxation and payments, creating recurring policy-driven repricing.
caseRest: The main risk is extreme price volatility, with annualised volatility around 48% and past cycle drawdowns exceeding 70% as leverage, liquidity and investor confidence reversed together. Losses can deepen when exchange failures or tighter regulation force investors to reduce exposure across otherwise distinct assets. Positive return skew does not make the allocation defensive because Bitcoin and Ether remain closely correlated during broad crypto sell-offs.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows Bitcoin’s return during the calendar month. Bitcoin is the largest digital asset and the main driver of a core crypto allocation, although Ether and smaller positions can produce different returns.

events.title: Cyprus Controls Accelerate Bitcoin Demand
events.text: Cyprus imposed bank controls during its financial rescue, increasing interest in assets held outside the banking system as Bitcoin rose 172%. The strategy gained because demand for Bitcoin broadened while the crypto market remained small and supply was limited.

events.title: Retail Demand Drives Bitcoin Higher
events.text: Retail participation and new futures contracts pushed Bitcoin up 39% during the final stage of its 2017 rally. The strategy gained because demand expanded faster than market liquidity, while Ether also benefited from initial coin offering activity.

events.title: Global Cash Rush Hits Digital Assets
events.text: The global rush for cash pushed Bitcoin down 25% as leveraged positions were liquidated across crypto exchanges. The strategy lost because digital assets traded as high-risk assets rather than safe havens, while Ether fell more sharply than Bitcoin.

events.title: China Crackdown Reverses Crypto Rally
events.text: China intensified restrictions on crypto trading and mining as Bitcoin fell 35% from an already extended valuation. The strategy lost because regulatory pressure prompted forced selling, reduced mining activity and weakened confidence across the digital asset market.

events.title: FTX Failure Deepens Crypto Losses
events.text: The failure of FTX pushed Bitcoin down 16% as customers withdrew assets and lenders reduced exposure to the sector. The strategy lost because counterparty concerns spread across exchanges, while forced liquidations weighed on Bitcoin and Ether together.

events.title: US Election Lifts Policy Expectations
events.text: The US election raised expectations for clearer digital asset rules and pushed Bitcoin up 37%. The strategy gained because investors anticipated broader institutional access, while strong exchange-traded fund flows supported demand for the largest assets.

instrument: Bitcoin and Ether held through regulated exchanges or physically backed products; cash held in Treasury bills
rules: Invest regularly; rebalance quarterly or when an asset moves 10 percentage points from target; exclude assets with weak liquidity or custody support
costs: Estimated trading spreads, custody charges and product fees deducted at each rebalance
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from digital asset adoption to disciplined risk control

legs.purpose: Captures adoption of the largest scarce digital asset
Captures growth in smart contracts and digital settlement
Funds rebalancing and limits forced sales

entry: Capital added monthly and allocated at the prevailing target weights
size: Total exposure capped at the strategic allocation, with no borrowing
exit: Asset removed if liquidity, custody access or network security deteriorates materially
stop: Rebalancing suspended during a custody failure or disorderly market closure
marketWatch: Institutional fund flows, stablecoin supply, exchange leverage and Bitcoin’s share of the crypto market indicate whether demand is broadening or becoming dependent on speculative positioning. Regulatory decisions, central bank meetings, protocol upgrades and major custody events matter because they can change access, liquidity and the discount rate applied to long-term adoption.

favourable.heading: Institutional access expands
favourable.text: Broader institutional access favours the strategy because regulated custody and exchange-traded products reduce operational barriers and bring new capital into a market with limited liquid supply. US spot Bitcoin fund approvals in January 2024 preceded strong inflows and a renewed rise in major digital assets.

favourable.heading: Monetary conditions ease
favourable.text: Easier monetary conditions favour the strategy because lower real yields support long-duration assets and make speculative capital more available. Bitcoin and Ether rose strongly after the policy response to the 2020 recession increased global liquidity and reduced interest rates.

favourable.heading: Network use broadens
favourable.text: Rising network use favours the strategy because higher settlement activity, stablecoin adoption and developer participation strengthen demand for block space and collateral. Ether benefited during 2020 and 2021 as decentralised finance and stablecoin activity expanded on its network.

adverse.heading: Liquidity tightens rapidly
adverse.text: Tighter liquidity hurts the strategy because higher real yields reduce demand for assets that produce no contractual cash flow and increase the cost of leveraged positions. Aggressive Federal Reserve tightening in 2022 coincided with a broad decline in Bitcoin, Ether and crypto credit.

adverse.heading: Regulation restricts market access
adverse.text: Restrictive regulation hurts the strategy because limits on trading, banking or custody reduce demand and can force miners and intermediaries to relocate. China’s 2021 restrictions on mining and trading contributed to a 35% monthly fall in Bitcoin.

adverse.heading: Counterparty failures force selling
adverse.text: Counterparty failures hurt the strategy because frozen withdrawals and impaired collateral spread losses across exchanges, lenders and investment funds. The collapse of FTX in November 2022 drove simultaneous declines in Bitcoin and Ether despite their separate networks.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s estimated return during each event using monthly Bitcoin, Ether and Treasury bill returns at the default weights. The calculation includes scheduled rebalancing and estimated trading and custody costs.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects moves in global liquidity, real yields, risk appetite and crypto leverage, which are then applied to Bitcoin, Ether and the cash reserve.

related.why: Follows crypto price trends and bears reversal risk rather than full-cycle market exposure.
Earns futures basis and bears exchange, funding and convergence risk instead of directional market risk.
Trades differences in crypto volatility and bears model, liquidity and tail risk.
